text: Friend, that shrine’s gone dark, but there’s smoke from the watchpost. Let’s see who’s keeping that fire. Era, let’s go talk to Bran at the watchpost. You got it. I’ll take us there. We’re off, boots crunching through snow toward Bran’s fire. I’ll mind the talk when we reach him, hero. You’re alive then. Good. Bran, warden of what’s left. The shrine fire went out three nights back when the barrow cracked open. I’m too old to go in after the ember stone. You’re not. Take this potion. You’ll want it. He’s tougher than he looks. We’re fresh, and I’ve a good recollection of those tomb drafts. Let’s shoulder what he can’t. Change your voice. Try a soft Irish one. Sure, just a breath. Soft it is, friend. Go on. I’m here. Ask him about the barrow. Yeah, let’s hear what he’ll say. The barrow was sealed before my grandmother was born. Three nights ago, the lintel cracked and the shrine fire went out the same hour. Whatever walked out of there took the ember stone with it. Then there’s our trail. We’ll go fetch what was stolen. What’s in my pack? Let me have a look for you. You’ve an iron sword and two health potions and a full breath in your chest. All right, take us to the shrine. Right, I’ll get us moving. Our boots crunch toward the standing stones, snow gathering on the old shoulders, and the air goes still.
